description: Wall-clock cost of one CFM training epoch, and the split between optimizer steps and the per-epoch held-out evaluation. Recorded to attribute the 2026-10-20 CPU-saturation report ('cpu跑满了') and to size the C7 full-corpus run. All numbers are epoch_time_sec from the trainer's own events.jsonl, not stopwatch readings of a shell wrapper.
split: train=512 val=192 (the two 512-cloud arms) and train=128 val=192 (the timing arm)

measurements.what: 512 clouds, 1 epoch, batch 64, gen_eval_n=0, six regularisers at their argparse defaults
byte-identical config to the PRE-FIX arm; only change is the Triton autotune key on _aggregate_vectors_kernel (n_edges,feat_dim) -> (feat_dim)
n_train 128 / val 192, same batch and regularisers; exists only to separate per-step cost from per-epoch eval cost

speedup.note: 304.302690 / 40.303891. Same config, same hardware, same six loss terms.

derived_split.method: two MEASURED points, 8 steps + E = 40.303891 and 2 steps + E = 24.654188; solve for the step and eval terms
derived_split.note: The trainer evaluates ONE CLOUD AT A TIME (evaluate_bond_accuracy + evaluate_decode_ratio each call model.forward per cloud), so eval cost scales with n_val, not with n_val/batch.

projection_full_corpus.basis: 26715 clouds / batch 64 = 418 steps at the DERIVED 2.608251 s/step, plus the DERIVED 19.44 s eval
projection_full_corpus.caveat: PROJECTED, not MEASURED: assumes per-step cost is flat in n_train (it should be, since each step touches a fixed 64 clouds) and that no epoch is slower for another reason (early-stop bookkeeping, checkpoint writes). The 5.55 h excludes the one-time ~90 s cohort load.

attribution.evidence: cProfile on the 2-step arm (pre-fix): 576 module forwards produced 981 autotune _bench calls — 109.4 s in triton.testing.do_bench and 40.1 s in torch._C._cuda_synchronize — out of 126.9 s of train_one_epoch.
attribution.why: _aggregate_vectors_kernel was autotuned with key=["n_edges", "feat_dim"]. The kernel launches grid=(n_edges,), one program per edge, and never loops over edges, so the optimal (num_warps, num_stages) cannot depend on n_edges. n_edges changes on every batch and on every eval cloud, so nearly every call re-benchmarked all 9 configs.

retractions.claim: 'Turning the six regularisers off costs 262.0 s vs 304.4 s, so the six terms are 14% of the epoch and are not the CPU bottleneck'
retractions.why: configs/c7_calib_noterms_2026_10_20.yaml set train.consistency_term_weight / so3_term_weight / edm_term_weight / shortcut_distill_term_weight, none of which resolves to a trainer dest. scripts/_config_binding_gate.py reported 4 VIOLATIONs on that file, so four of the seven keys never left the argparse defaults and the terms stayed ON. The 42 s delta was autotune-cache variance between two runs, not the regularisers. The config was deleted rather than repaired: the user's standing instruction is that all six terms stay on.

retractions.claim: 'fm_ode alone accounts for 12% of the epoch (269.1 s vs 304.4 s)'
retractions.why: Same pre-fix regime: 86% of the epoch was autotune benchmarking, so a 35 s difference between two single-epoch runs is within the run-to-run autotune noise. train.fm_ode_term_weight DOES resolve to a dest, so that arm did turn the term off — the measurement was real, the attribution was not.

retractions.claim: '_build_bond_pair_features (per-edge Python loop, .cpu().tolist()) is the CPU hotspot in the train step'
retractions.why: _build_bond_pair_features does not appear in the cProfile output at all: this trainer never calls adapter.train_step, it runs its own inline FM block, so that function is dead on this path. The per-edge Python loop is real but unexercised here.
